_readme: How much you want to work somewhere, 0-5. Copy to company_affinity.json
and edit that copy - the real list is gitignored, this example is tracked.
This is the one input the scorer cannot infer. Everything else it reads
off the posting; this is the part only you know.
Scale, and what each step is worth out of the component's 17 points:
5 -> 17   would drop everything for this one
4 -> 14   actively want it
3 -> 10   happy to work there
2 ->  7   neutral (the fallback for a company with no rating and no tier)
1 ->  3   would take it if nothing better
0 ->  0   would not apply
Resolution order: your rating wins. Failing that, an ats-search registry
tier seeds it (tier 1 -> 4, 2 -> 3, 3 -> 2, 4-5 -> 1). Only a company with
neither falls back to `default`. So a rating is never *required* - it is
how you overrule the tier when the tier is not what you actually feel.
Rating one company lifts every posting it has, together. That is the point:
you rate employers, not postings, and the board reorders itself.
Names are matched leniently - legal suffixes and punctuation are stripped,
then token overlap must reach `company.match_threshold` in fit_profile.
'DeepJudge AG' matches 'DeepJudge'. The matched name is written into the
row's fit_reasons so a wrong match is visible rather than silent.
